newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia 1996 GDP rose by 1.6 pct. [CORRECTED 17:58 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Macedonia 1996 GDP rose by 1.6 pct. [CORRECTED 17:58 GMT]

text.p: Macedonia's 1996 gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 1.6 percent after a 1.4 percent decline in 1995, the National Bank of Macedonia said.

NBM officials attributed the initial economic recovery to the effect of stabilisation and structural reform policies sustained by the government and the backing of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.

Trade links and foreign participation have picked up last year after neighbouring Greece lifted a crippling 18-month trade blockade in October 1995 and the United Nations lifted sanctions on neighboring Serbia and Montenegro, enabling Macedonian companies to restore partial ties with their traditional markets.

Macedonia's industrial output fell 10.3 percent in December 1996 (corrects from "last year") due to ongoing restructuring and privatisation of state enterprises. Factories have yet to find new sources of investment after the government has cut budget funding in line with World Bank recommendations. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
